checksum_sha256.description: The declared SHA-256 as 64 hex digits; empty declares no checksum

content_type.description: The media type the bytes will carry; must be non-blank. The upload records it as the object's mime.

name.description: An optional label for the object; normalized before storing, and omitted or empty stores an empty name

size.description: The object's size in bytes; must be positive, and the upload's byte count must equal it exactly. A declaration without a positive size is refused whole.

ObjectstoreObject.description: One object as the routes expose it: the values observed by the last upload plus the row's timestamps. It never carries the internal storage key, and every instant is UTC.

checksum_sha256.description: The SHA-256 of the stored bytes as 64 lowercase hex digits, computed during the last upload; empty until the first upload lands.

created_at.description: When the object was declared, as an RFC 3339 instant in UTC.

expires_at.description: When a completed object will be swept into deleted, written from object-ttl at completion; absent when no lifetime is configured, so the object does not expire.

id.description: The object's identifier, minted at declaration; every other object route takes it in the path.

mime.description: The content type recorded by the last upload, taken from the declared content_type; empty until the first upload lands.

name.description: The declared label, normalized once when the object was created; empty when none was declared or it normalized to nothing

size.description: The observed byte count recorded by the last upload; zero until the first upload lands.

state.description: The lifecycle state: pending after declaration, uploaded once bytes are stored, completed after the completion call, deleted once tombstoned. A deleted object reads as 404 on every route except delete.

updated_at.description: When the row last changed, whether by declaration, upload, completion or deletion, as an RFC 3339 instant in UTC.

Problem.description: An RFC 9457 problem document. This is the entry point's default error shape, which a host-supplied ErrorResponder may replace.

detail.description: A longer explanation of this occurrence, present only when the answering module has one to give. It may be a sentence rendered in the request language or a language-neutral token such as "forbidden", so clients must not parse it.

instance.description: A URI identifying this occurrence; absent when there is none to give.

status.description: The HTTP status code the response is written with, repeated from the status line.

title.description: A short summary of the kind of problem. A module that sets none gets the standard English status text for the status code.

type.description: The machine-readable code identifying the kind of problem. A module that sets none gets the RFC 9457 default about:blank; codes this platform defines are URNs of the form urn:speed:<capability>:<code>.

get.description: Lists this tenant's objects that are not deleted, ordered by creation instant and then identifier, both ascending. The cursor is opaque and continues after the last row of the previous page, so rows written while a caller pages do not shift rows already read. limit defaults to 50 rows when absent or zero; a negative limit, one above 200, a non-numeric limit or a cursor this module did not write is refused whole with a 400. A database failure is answered 503.

parameters.description: Continue after the last row of the previous page; absent or empty starts at the first page
parameters.name: cursor

parameters.description: Cap on the page size; the metadata module applies a default and an upper bound
parameters.name: limit

schema.description: One page of the tenant's undeleted objects; next_cursor is empty when the page was not full.

next_cursor.description: The cursor to pass on the next call; empty when the page was not full, meaning no further page is known.

objects.description: The page's objects, at most limit of them, ordered by creation instant and then identifier, both ascending.

200.description: A page of objects and the cursor of the page's last row

400.description: The cursor or limit is not readable

503.description: The object store could not answer

get.summary: One page of the tenant's undeleted objects

post.description: Declares an object: validates the declaration, normalizes the name once, mints the object identifier and lands a pending row, with an upload window opened from the configured upload-window. size must be positive, content_type must be non-blank, and checksum_sha256 is either empty or 64 hex digits; a declaration that fails any of these is refused whole and lands no row. An omitted, empty or reduced-to-nothing name stores as an empty string rather than failing. The response is the pending view: its size, mime and checksum_sha256 are not filled in until the first upload records them.

requestBody.description: The object declaration, as a JSON object.

schema.description: The view of the object just declared; it is pending and its observed size, mime and checksum_sha256 are not filled in yet.

400.description: The body is not a JSON object or the declaration is not readable

415.description: The request body is not application/json

503.description: The object store could not answer

post.summary: Declare an object and open its upload window

delete.description: Removes the object's bytes through the byte backend and tombstones its row with state deleted. An object already deleted is a success that touches no byte, so a repeat is idempotent. A byte-backend failure leaves the row unchanged and answers 503. An unknown identifier or another tenant's object is answered 404.

parameters.description: The object's identifier. An object already deleted is a success, so a repeat needs no different handling.
parameters.name: id

204.description: The object was deleted, or was already deleted

404.description: No object this tenant can see carries that id

503.description: The object store could not answer

delete.summary: Remove an object's bytes and tombstone its row

get.description: Returns one object's view. A deleted object is answered exactly like an unknown identifier or another tenant's object, with a 404, so the response does not reveal whether the object existed. The view never carries the internal storage key, and every instant is UTC.

parameters.description: The object's identifier, as returned at declaration. An identifier this tenant cannot see, whether unknown, another tenant's or deleted, is answered 404.
parameters.name: id

schema.description: The view of the requested object.

404.description: No object this tenant can see carries that id

503.description: The object store could not answer

post.description: Moves an uploaded object to completed and writes expires_at from the configured object-ttl, leaving it absent when no lifetime is configured; the object's bytes become readable. A pending object was never uploaded and is a 409; an already-completed object is returned unchanged with its expiry as it was, so a repeat is idempotent. A deleted object, an unknown identifier or another tenant's object is a 404.

parameters.description: The identifier of an object to move to completed; one already completed is returned unchanged.
parameters.name: id

schema.description: The view of the object after the call; a repeat on an already-completed object returns it unchanged.

404.description: No object this tenant can see carries that id

409.description: The object's state does not allow the action

503.description: The object store could not answer

get.description: Streams a completed object's bytes with the Content-Type taken from the mime the object recorded at upload, falling back to application/octet-stream when the object records none. Only a completed object can be read: pending or uploaded is a 409, while deleted, unknown or another tenant's is a 404. A completed row whose bytes are missing from the backend is a 503. No Content-Disposition is set; a client that wants a filename takes the view's name.

parameters.description: The identifier of a completed object whose bytes are to be read.
parameters.name: id

200.description: The object's bytes, written with the media type the object recorded

404.description: No object this tenant can see carries that id

503.description: The object store could not answer

get.summary: The object's bytes, streamed with the object's recorded media type

put.description: Stores the request body as the object's bytes under the internal key. The request's Content-Length must be present and equal the declared size: a request that names no length, or whose length differs, is refused before any byte is stored. The object must be pending or uploaded and its upload window must still be open: a completed object or a closed window is a 409, and a deleted object or one this tenant cannot see is a 404. A successful upload records the observed size and SHA-256 and moves the object to uploaded; re-uploading a pending or uploaded object replaces its bytes under the same key.

parameters.description: The identifier of a pending or uploaded object whose upload window is still open.
parameters.name: id

requestBody.description: The object's bytes, as the raw request body.

400.description: The request names no Content-Length, or its length does not match the declaration

404.description: No object this tenant can see carries that id

409.description: The object's state does not allow the action, or its upload window has closed

415.description: The request body is not application/octet-stream

503.description: The object store could not answer

put.summary: Store the request body as the object's bytes
